mainEntity.name: Why is pregnancy counted from my last period, not conception?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first day of the last period is usually a known date, while conception usually isn't. Counting from the LMP adds about two weeks before conception, which is why a full-term pregnancy is described as 40 weeks.

mainEntity.name: What if my cycles are irregular?

acceptedAnswer.text: LMP-based dates are less reliable with irregular or unknown cycles. An early ultrasound gives a more accurate estimate, and your provider will usually date the pregnancy from it.

Yes. If an early ultrasound measurement differs from your LMP date by more than ACOG's thresholds, your provider may update your due date. Once set from an early scan, it usually isn't changed by later scans.
